newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end higher on New York gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end higher on New York gains.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures closed higher across the board on Friday, as overnight gains in New York encouraged local investors to buy, traders said.
Prices ranged from 17 to 24 yen higher, with benchmark June 1998 finishing up 19 yen at 1,195 yen per gram.
The New York gold market ended higher overnight, led by gold buying by funds, trade houses and commission houses.
"The gains in New York encouraged local investors here," a trader said.
Bullion was quoted at $323.50/324.00 per ounce at 0745 GMT, compared to $323.00/40 in early Friday Asian trade.
Yen-based platinum futures ended mixed, with prices ranging from 13 yen lower to six yen higher. Benchmark June 1998 ended one yen higher at 1,357 yen per gram.
Traders said they were watching whether Russian platinum exports reach Japan next week, as Russia's platinum group metal export agency told Japanese clients.
"A lesson we learnt from Russia this year is to trust but verify. We won't trust them until platinum actually arrives," a trading house trader said.
Palladium futures closed lower. Benchmark June 1998 was down one yen at 535 yen per gram.
Silver futures closed higher reflecting overnight gains in New York, traders said. The June 1998 was up 2.0 yen at 161.5 yen per 10 grams.
